messages:
maya (sec): Quick alert: plan to remove a set of risky capabilities from our base images (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, CAP_NET_RAW) and strip setuid binaries. Need runbook updates, RBAC/IAM review for signing, audit log coverage, and a safe rollout path. Thoughts?
fern (infra): +1. We should run discovery first to find workloads that explicitly add caps or rely on setuid. I'll kick off a scan. Suggest these checks: 1) list pods with securityContext.capabilities.add 2) scan images for suid files 3) find hostNetwork/hostPID uses.
zhou (eng-runtime): Helpful kubectl one-liners:```
# pods with added caps
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o jsonpath="{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.metadata.name} {.spec.containers[*].securityContext.capabilities.add}
{end}" | grep -v "<none>"
# init containers
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o jsonpath="{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.metadata.name} {.spec.initContainers[*].securityContext.capabilities.add}
{end}" | grep -v "<none>"
```Also, image scanning for suid: run a privileged DaemonSet with `find / -perm /4000 -type f -print` and report. Run in dev first.
kevin (platform): Signing/KMS: we need to decide per-team vs org key. Recommend per-team keys to limit blast radius. Requirements: each key must have Data Access audit logs enabled, a signer principal (build SA) with only cryptoKeySign, and logs forwarded to SIEM with image name+digest fields.
maya (sec): Agree per-team. Also need to ensure consent on re-signing policy when keys are rotated. Add to runbook: rotate quarterly or after major rebuild and trigger a resign job for production images.
fern (infra): On audit logs: remember Data Access logs for KMS are off by default. I'll verify and enable for new keys. Also ensure cosign usage via Workload Identity or short-lived tokens, not long-lived JSON keys.
zhou (eng-runtime): For rollout, I propose a four-stage flow: 1) inventory & notify owners 2) deploy Gatekeeper/OPA policy in audit mode (2 weeks) 3) rebuild base images, sign them with team keys and publish to canary namespaces 4) flip to deny in admission controller after canaries pass for 72h.
kevin (platform): I'll produce a TF module for per-team keys + IAM role binding to build SAs and add a logging sink to security project. Will include a snippet to enable DATA_ACCESS audit logs for the keys.
maya (sec): Failure modes: owners need a rollback path if an app depends on net capabilities. Plan: admission controller whitelist for an 'escape' namespace, and maintain a small set of runtime-compatible model images with reduced caps as temporary fallback. Add a postmortem template if rollout causes outages.
fern (infra): Starting the cluster scan now. Will include hostNetwork/hostPID/privileged checks. Expect results in a few hours.
oncall-bot: Reminder: SEC-700 created and assigned to fern (infra). Due 2024-10-28.
zhou (eng-runtime): Small note on signing command for cosign+KMS:```
COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=1 cosign sign --key gcpkms://projects/<proj>/locations/global/keyRings/<kr>/cryptoKeys/<key> image:sha256:<digest>
```Make sure builder runs under the SA with only sign permission.
kevin (platform): I'll open PR with TF and a sample IAM policy, pinging maya for review.
maya (sec): Thanks all. Action items: fern: inventory scan + report; kevin: TF PR; zhou: gatekeeper audit policy in staging; I'll draft enforcement decision criteria and runbook updates. Watch the ticket SEC-700 for updates. :thumbsup:
